newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end dismally, uncertainty reign.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end dismally, uncertainty reign.

text.p: Singapore shares ended dismally on Friday with investors sidelined, dealers said.
"I'm not telling any of my clients to buy at the moment. The market's too uncertain," said a dealer with a local firm.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index closed down 26.95 points at 2.068.48, wiping 1.3 percent off its value.

An unexpected dip of 7.9 percent in February's year-on-year non-oil domestic exports announced on Thursday, disappointing corporate results and concerns over possible U.S. interest rate rises combined to hit the market hard, dealers said.
However dealers saw retrenchment below 2,050 as unlikely.
"I really don't see a retreat below that because we were quite underweighted when the fall started," a dealer said.

Keppel Corp stock -- a barometer for the economy -- sank to a three-year low of Singapore $9.05 before perking to S$9.20, down S$0.25, while Great Eastern Life and City Development warrants both lost a dollar to S$21.40 and S$10.00 respectively.
Gains were few -- 77 to 303 losers on volume of 186.9 million shares -- led by Samanda Holdings, up S$0.60 at S$9.10.
"There are buyers, but they're lying low and not buying index stocks," one dealer complained.
